text:
sophie: Heads-up — between 14:02 and 14:18 UTC we saw a small spike of `DECRYPT_FAILURE` errors in prod (service: inference-edge). About ~0.8% of requests in that window returned transient KMS timeouts and fell back to local DEK cache. Not seeing user-facing errors but want to triage. Logs attached below.
ops-sre: can you paste a sample log line? which KMS (aws/gcp/az)?
sophie: pasted one: `2026-03-19T14:05:07Z ERROR decrypt failed key=projects/infra/locations/us-central1/keyRings/ring/cryptoKeys/redwood DECRYPT_TIMEOUT status=504 attempts=3 fallback=local-dek-cache` — looks like GCP KMS in us-central1.
sec-bot: Incident record created: INC-2026-034. Initial classification: near-miss; availability impact mitigated by envelope cache fallback.
alex: curious — did rotation happen recently? if cache had a stale DEK that could be risky.
sophie: no scheduled rotation in last 24h. Key metadata shows last rotation 11 days ago. DEK cache TTL is 72h for that service, so it's not stale.
maria: also saw increased API latencies for some customers in the same window but not 5xx. might correlate.
ryan: what's the fallback path? do we call KMS envelope decrypt then cache plaintext key? codepath is `decryptEnvelope()` -> if KMS errors then `getCachedDEK()` -> decrypt locally.
kevin: that's right. We intentionally cache plaintext DEKs in memory for short TTL to survive brief KMS blips. But we should audit when fallback happens.
sophie: currently we log `fallback=local-dek-cache` but that log isn't exported to our audit sink. Good catch.
ops-sre: root-cause hunting — is this KMS throttling, regional networking, or our client library? Can we repro with a synthetic load against GCP endpoint?
alex: I ran a quick curl-based probe to the GCP KMS endpoint and saw increased TCP connect times in us-central1 at ~14:04-14:06. Spark in Cloud-NAT metrics around same time.
maria: also noticed that a recent RBAC tweak removed the `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` from the fallback agent pool in us-central1 for ~20 minutes due to a terraform drift, but was reverted quickly. Could that line up?
ryan: if RBAC was revoked then KMS would respond 403 rather than timeout. logs show 504/timeouts, not 403s.
sophie: exactly — RBAC change seems unrelated, but worth noting timeline overlap.
kevin: two hypotheses: network egress issue to GCP KMS (connectivity) OR a transient KMS backend throttling spike. GCP status doesn't show an outage.
ops-sre: mitigation checklist: 1) ensure fallback logging is exported to audit sink with an event indicating `decryption_used_cache=true` 2) add a circuit-breaker around KMS calls so we fail fast and reduce retry storm 3) increase jitter/backoff seeds for KMS client 4) add per-region request counters + alerting.
maria: +1 on audit event. We need to be able to answer "was user's data decrypted with a cached key" for compliance.
sec-bot: Action added: INC-2026-034-A1: export fallback audit events to Splunk, priority P1. Assignee: sophie. Due: 2026-03-20 18:00 UTC.
sophie: started a small PR: `log/audit: emit fallback_event{service,inference-edge,key_id,region,cached_ttl_remaining}`. Pushing to ci.
alex: we should also fail closed for high-risk tenants (enterprise plan) — i.e., if fallback happens for enterprise customers, surface an error instead of silent fallback. flag `require_kms_online=true` on tenant config.
kevin: agree. Need to coordinate with product. For now we'll add an annotation to the audit event with tenant tier.
ryan: quick config lesson learned: DEK cache TTL (72h) > key rotation grace (48h) — that could allow decrypt-with-old-DEK after key rotation if we rotate envelope keys. We should ensure rotation scheme invalidates cached DEKs or uses key versioning in cache keys.
maria: we do include key version in cache key for DEK lookup, but older versions may still be cached if rotation replaced DEK but we didn't purge. Add purge on rotate event.
ops-sre: temporary mitigation deployed at 14:50 UTC: reduced KMS client max concurrent requests from 100->40 in us-central1, added per-client 50ms jitter. Observed k8s pod CPU spike decayed. Since then error rate down to baseline.
sec-bot: NOTE: related RBAC drift ticket TF-349 reopened for investigation. Linking.
alex: long-term: implement multi-kms routing (try alternative region earlier) and allow soft-fail policy: if region KMS degraded then route to secondary region KMS with review flag — must evaluate data sovereignty impact.
kevin: also want a synthetic canary that calls `decrypt` once per minute and emits 1m histogram to SLO dashboard. If errors >0.1% over 10m trigger alert.
sophie: filed follow-ups: 1) audit export PR (in review); 2) circuit-breaker/short-circuit PR (WIP); 3) add canary + dashboard (ticket created). I'll post links when available.
ops-sre: product ask: add tenant opt-in for strict mode (no-cache fallback). Ticket to product: PROD-1012.
ryan: tests to add: simulate KMS timeouts and ensure fallback event emitted and that we don't silently proceed for strict tenants. Add unit + e2e.
maria: small ops note — check Azure Key Vault and AWS KMS metrics too; last week we saw minor egress NAT saturation affecting multi-cloud egress.
kevin: FYI, encryption library v2.3.1 had exponential backoff bug (no jitter) — we backported fix in 2.3.2 yesterday. Confirm everyone on latest?
sophie: inference-edge is on 2.3.2 prod. older edge workers on canary cluster still 2.3.1; patching now.
sec-bot: Closing summary: near-miss due to transient GCP KMS timeouts. Mitigations: fallback audit logging, circuit-breaker, jitter/backoff tuning, canary + dashboard, tenant strict mode opt-in, rotation/purge improvements. Actions assigned. Reopen if errors resurface.
ops-sre: thanks all. If anyone sees `fallback=local-dek-cache` in prod without an associated audit event after deploy, ping me.
sophie: will follow up with PR links and retrospective notes.
ryan: I'll add unit tests for the rotation/purge logic.
kevin: I'll schedule a runbook update for fallback behavior and include how to verify audit events.
maria: reassigning TF-349 to infra-security for RBAC drift root-cause analysis.
sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-034 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Will update if severity changes.
